kinds.name: Old town
kinds.description: Historic streets, tight-knit community groups — but older buildings make retrofits trickier.

kinds.name: Apartment blocks
kinds.description: Dense housing with big heating bills; the largest retrofit payoff in town.

kinds.name: Suburb
kinds.description: Family homes with large roofs and lawns, built around the car.

kinds.name: Riverside
kinds.description: Tight against the water; flood risk in wet years and real wetland potential.

kinds.name: Industrial edge
kinds.description: Workshops and empty mills with big, flat roofs calling out for solar.

kinds.name: Retail park
kinds.description: Vast car parks — prime ground for solar canopies, short on public life.

kinds.name: Farmland
kinds.description: Grows more food than it uses; hungry for a local market and healthy soil.

kinds.name: Woodland
kinds.description: A habitat reserve that quietly protects its neighbours' biodiversity.

kinds.name: Ksar
kinds.description: The old fortified village of earth houses and narrow shaded lanes; cool walls, but crumbling where nobody lives any more.

kinds.name: Palm gardens
kinds.description: Gardens in layers under the date palms, watered by channels the families have kept for generations.

kinds.name: New quarter
kinds.description: Newer concrete houses along the road: easy to build, but hot in summer and hungry for water and power.

kinds.name: Market square
kinds.description: The souk, the minibus stop and the cafés: where everyone passes through.

kinds.name: Herders' edge
kinds.description: Where the oasis meets the open land: herders, goats, and fields that need every drop of rain.
